route_note: R1 with the record's 'direct launch' (cheaper legitimate variant), same for both variants: the kernel template generic_kernel_col_reduction_2d_blocked is taken from the checked-out revision's own header (common/cuda_hip/base/kernel_launch_reduction.hpp via common/unified/base/kernel_launch_reduction.hpp with GKO_COMPILING_CUDA / GKO_DEVICE_NAMESPACE=cuda, nothing copied or edited) and launched directly from driver.cu with grid (1,1), rows 8, cols 64. The full Ginkgo library is NOT built. The project's own CMake CONFIGURE step (no build) generates include/ginkgo/config.hpp and the CUDA backend's flags (cfg/cuda/CMakeFiles/ginkgo_cuda.dir/flags.make); the driver is compiled with exactly those: -O3 -DNDEBUG -std=c++17 --generate-code=arch=compute_89,code=[compute_89,sm_89] -Xcompiler=-fPIC --expt-relaxed-constexpr --expt-extended-lambda, the backend's defines (GKO_COMPILING_CUDA, GKO_DEVICE_NAMESPACE=cuda, THRUST_*) and include list, plus -lineinfo (CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES derived from $RW_NVCC_FLAGS; configure options: CUDA only, tests/examples/benchmarks/MPI/OMP/HIP/SYCL OFF; no network needed). The record's CUDA 13 worry did not materialise: this Sept-2026 revision compiles unchanged with nvcc 13.4 / gcc 12.4. An RPATH to the gcc-12.4 lib64 (libstdc++) is added at link; the driver is otherwise static (CUDA runtime static). The -lineinfo SASS check of route R1 is owned by helper C: see targets/hecbench-dxtc2-1/lineinfo.check (RESULT SAME).
driver: driver.cu: allocates a double[64] result, launches gko::kernels::cuda::generic_kernel_col_reduction_2d_blocked<<<dim3(1,1), default_block_size>>>(rows=8, cols=64, rw_fn (row+col), rw_op (+), rw_fin (identity), identity 0.0, result), checks result[c] == 28 + 8*c. default_block_size is 512 at this revision (record said 256), warp_size 32, so the column-block loop (col_step = gridDim.y*32 = 32) runs twice. Prints 'ginkgo-1 driver: default_block_size=512 warp_size=32 rows=8 cols=64 grid=(1,1)' and 'ginkgo-1 driver: 0 of 64 columns differ from the reference OK'.
input: 1 block of 512 threads, 2 loop iterations: per iteration 512 STS + 512 LDS (warp 0 reads all 512 entries, 16 per lane) + 32 STG, so about 2.1e3 shared/global accesses (counted from the code), far below 1e7.

The record's 'grid (1,1), 256 threads' was adjusted to the revision's real block size 512 because block_partial and the warp-0 read loop are sized by default_block_size.
